title: ROLLUP
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server ROLLUP operator to generate hierarchical grouping sets for subtotals and totals.

data.text: The ROLLUP operator is a subclause of the GROUP BY clause that provides a shorthand for defining multiple grouping sets based on a hierarchy among the dimension columns. Unlike CUBE, which generates all possible combinations, ROLLUP only generates grouping sets that follow the specified hierarchy.
ROLLUP assumes a hierarchy among the dimension columns and only generates grouping sets based on this hierarchy. This makes it ideal for generating subtotals and totals for reporting purposes.

data.title: CUBE vs ROLLUP Grouping Sets
data.content: Comparing the grouping sets generated by CUBE and ROLLUP for three columns.
data.code:
-- CUBE(d1, d2, d3) produces 8 grouping sets:
(d1, d2, d3)
(d1, d2)
(d2, d3)
(d1, d3)
(d1)
(d2)
(d3)
()

-- ROLLUP(d1, d2, d3) produces 4 grouping sets:
(d1, d2, d3)
(d1, d2)
(d1)
()

data.title: ROLLUP Syntax
data.content: Calculates aggregates based on a hierarchical grouping of dimension columns.
data.code:
SELECT
    d1,
    d2,
    d3,
    aggregate_function(c4)
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    ROLLUP(d1, d2, d3);

data.text: In this syntax, d1, d2, and d3 are dimension columns. The statement calculates the aggregation of values in column c4 based on the hierarchy d1 > d2 > d3. You can also perform a partial roll-up by combining regular columns with ROLLUP.

data.title: Partial ROLLUP
data.content: Applies ROLLUP to only a subset of the grouping columns.
data.code:
SELECT
    d1,
    d2,
    d3,
    aggregate_function(c4)
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    d1,
    ROLLUP(d2, d3);

data.text: The following query calculates sales amounts by brand (subtotal) and by both brand and category (total), using the sales.sales_summary table.

data.title: ROLLUP with Brand and Category
data.content: Calculates sales subtotals by brand and a grand total by brand and category.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    ROLLUP(brand, category);

data.alt: SQL Server ROLLUP example output showing subtotals and totals

data.text: The query assumes a hierarchy between brand and category: brand > category. If you change the order of the columns, the hierarchy and results change accordingly.

data.title: ROLLUP with Reversed Column Order
data.content: Reversing the column order changes the hierarchy from category > brand.
data.code:
SELECT
    category,
    brand,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    ROLLUP(category, brand);

data.alt: SQL Server ROLLUP example with reversed column order

data.title: ROLLUP Key Points
points: ROLLUP generates hierarchical grouping sets based on a specified column hierarchy.
For N columns, ROLLUP produces N+1 grouping sets (fewer than CUBE's 2^N).
ROLLUP is ideal for generating subtotals and grand totals in reports.
The order of columns in ROLLUP determines the hierarchy of the grouping sets.
